title: Resultar + adjective: the legacy of the caudillos

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *resultar* + adjective from B1 Unit 15: it says how something turned out to be. It is a good way to talk about a legacy: what turned out to be difficult, useful or dangerous. The adjective agrees with the thing described.

sections.title: Resultar + adjective
rows: *resultó* + adjective + infinitive: it turned out to be difficult to create
the adjective agrees with the subject (masculine singular)

items.english: It turned out to be difficult to create strong institutions.

items.spanish: Un jefe fuerte resultó útil para mantener el orden.
items.english: A strong chief turned out to be useful for keeping order.

items.spanish: El poder personal resultó peligroso para la democracia.
items.english: Personal power turned out to be dangerous for democracy.

items.spanish: Las leyes resultaban débiles en el campo.
items.english: The laws turned out to be weak in the countryside.

sections.content: With an infinitive, *resultar* stays singular and the adjective stays masculine: *resultó difícil crear instituciones*. With a noun, both agree: *las leyes resultaron débiles*. Use the preterite (*resultó*) for the final result and the imperfect (*resultaba*) for how things were over time.
